title: Scalar finite-projective dual realization on a ringed site
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $B$ be a sheaf of commutative rings equipped with a morphism $\underline R\to B$, where underlines denote constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived category $D(B)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Set $C_B(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$ for ordinary $R$-modules, using ordinary sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $F^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of finite projective $R$-modules, with degreewise finite-free retract data [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], and put $E^\bullet=C_B(F^\bullet)$ termwise. Define $F^{\vee,\bullet}=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(F^\bullet,R[0])$ with
$$(F^{\vee,\bullet})^q=\operatorname{Hom}_R(F^{-q},R),\qquad d^q(\phi)=-(-1)^q\phi\,d_F^{-q-1}$$
[def-pur-hom-complex]. Each $E^q$ is a direct summand of a finite free $B$-module sheaf, and $\mathcal Hom_B(E^q,-)$ is exact. For every K-injective resolution $B[0]\to I^\bullet$, the comparison
$$\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,B[0])\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,I^\bullet)$$
is a quasi-isomorphism, so its source represents $R\mathcal Hom_B(E^\bullet,B)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For every finite projective $R$-module $V$, the canonical sheaf morphism
$$\beta_V:C_B(\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R))\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_B(C_B(V),B),\qquad \beta_V(b\otimes\phi)(b'\otimes v)=bb'\phi(v)$$
is an isomorphism natural in $V$. Applied to $V=F^{-q}$, these maps form an isomorphism of cochain complexes
$$C_B(F^{\vee,\bullet})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E^\bullet,B[0]),$$
with the displayed signed differentials, hence give a natural isomorphism $C_B(F^{\vee,\bullet})\simeq R\mathcal Hom_B(E^\bullet,B)$ in $D(B)$. If $F^\bullet$ is zero outside $[a,b]$, both dual complexes are zero outside $[-b,-a]$. No flatness of $B$ over $\underline R$ is assumed.

proof.text: The constant-module and tensor universal properties make $C_B$ additive: maps act by $b\otimes v\mapsto b\otimes f(v)$, so identity, composition and addition hold on local generators and hence after sheafification. The finite-free scalar-identification lemma gives $C_B(R^N)\cong B^N$, including rank zero, without flatness. Applying this functor to each supplied $p_ri_r=1$ gives the required finite-free retracts for $E^r$. Since $C_B(0)=0$, $E$ retains the bounds of $F$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, scalar finite-free reduction and supplied splittings

proof.text: For every $r$, apply the finite-retract internal-dual exactness lemma to the splitting of $E^r$ from step 1. It gives exactness of $\mathcal Hom_B(E^r,-)$ on module sheaves, without claiming exactness of global sections.

The scalar-evaluation descent lemma gives $\beta_V$ with exactly the displayed formula and contravariant naturality for every scalar module. For finite projective $V$, apply the normalized-inverse lemma to this $\beta_V$. Its dual-generator formula supplies a restriction-compatible two-sided inverse, independent of the splitting.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, scalar evaluation and inverse

proof.text: Apply signed cochain assembly with $T=C_B$ and $\eta_V=\beta_V$. Step 1 supplies additivity, step 3 supplies naturality and invertibility on every $F^r$. It gives the natural signed isomorphism to $D(E,B)$ and both reversed bounds. The existing Hom-to-single isomorphism identifies $D(E,B)$ with $\mathcal Hom_B^\bullet(E,B[0])$; its differential is the same $-(-1)^q$ precomposition formula. Projection to the unique nonzero factor commutes with precomposition, since that factor sends a cochain map $f$ to precomposition by $f^{-q}$; thus this presentation change is natural.

source.place: Tags 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, and 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, signed dual

proof.text: By steps 1--2, $E$ is bounded and its termwise internal Hom functors are exact. Apply the bounded-exact-term Hom lemma to any K-injective resolution $B[0]\to I$: its statement allows arbitrary unbounded target complexes, so it gives the asserted quasi-isomorphism for every such resolution. By the definition of derived internal Hom its target represents $R\mathcal Hom_B(E,B)$. Localize the cochain isomorphism from step 4 and compose with this comparison in $D(B)$. The fixed functorial resolution gives naturality in $F$; canonical independence of resolution identifies all other choices with it. No tensor-exactness or flatness assumption was used.
